tagline: Protecting Families Through Affordable Life and Health Insurance
hero_kpi_rationale: The underwriting margin is the primary indicator of operating performance in life insurance and the key profitability measure used by management. It represents the difference between premiums and costs related to claims and acquisition, reflecting the efficiency of the core business model.

kpis.name: Life and Health Underwriting Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between premiums and costs related to claims and acquisition.
kpis.description: Total underwriting margin (life + health) increased by 8% in 2025, driven by premium growth and disciplined cost management. Life insurance underwriting margin reached $1,509 million and health insurance underwriting margin reached $390 million.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in insurance underwriting margin

kpis.name: Life Insurance Premiums
kpis.explanation: Revenue from collected life insurance premiums.
kpis.description: Life insurance premiums reached $3.4 billion in 2025, up 3% compared to 2024.

kpis.name: Health Insurance Premiums
kpis.explanation: Revenue from collected health insurance premiums.
kpis.description: Health premiums increased by 9% in 2025, rising from $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion.

kpis.name: Net Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Core earnings of the company, excluding non-recurring items and realized gains/losses.
kpis.description: Net operating income reached $1.20 billion in 2025, an 8% increase compared to 2024.
kpis.signal: Strong increase in net operating income

kpis.name: Operating ROE excluding AOCI
kpis.explanation: Return on operating equity, excluding fluctuations in capital reserves.
kpis.description: Operating ROE, excluding AOCI, was 16.0% in 2025, confirming the strength of the business model. Management typically targets a 'mid-teens' range.
kpis.signal: Operating ROE stable within target range

kpis.short: Book Value per Share excl AOCI
kpis.name: Book Value per Share excluding AOCI
kpis.explanation: Adjusted book value per share, excluding capital reserves.
kpis.description: Book value per share, excluding AOCI, increased by 11% in 2025, rising from $86.40 to $96.16.

kpis.name: Total Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total amount of new policies sold, net of cancellations.
kpis.description: Total net sales increased by 13% in 2025, rising from $840 million to $948 million.

kpis.name: Average Producing Agents
kpis.explanation: Average number of agents who generated sales during the year.
kpis.description: The average number of producing agents increased by 3% in 2025. Exclusive divisions (American Income 11,920, Liberty National 3,846, Family Heritage 1,527, United American 4,396) totaled approximately 21,689 agents.

kpis.name: Total Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total amount of new policies sold, net of cancellations.
kpis.description: Total net sales increased by 13% in 2025, rising from $840 million to $948 million.

kpis.name: Health Insurance Premiums
kpis.explanation: Revenue from collected health insurance premiums.
kpis.description: Health premiums increased by 9% in 2025, rising from $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion.

kpis.short: Book Value per Share excl AOCI
kpis.name: Book Value per Share excluding AOCI
kpis.explanation: Adjusted book value per share, excluding capital reserves.
kpis.description: Book value per share, excluding AOCI, increased by 11% in 2025, rising from $86.40 to $96.16.

risks.title: Interest Rate Risk
risks.score_rationale: Interest rate risk is high due to the sensitivity of the company's investments to interest rate fluctuations. Invested assets are significant and sensitive to yield changes. The AOCI adjustment of ($1.8) billion in 2025 reflects this exposure.

risks.title: Credit Risk
risks.score_rationale: Credit risk is moderate due to the quality of the company's investments. Investment stability in 2025 and a diversified portfolio limit significant exposure.

risks.title: Competitive Risk
risks.score_rationale: Competitive risk is high due to the presence of numerous players in the insurance market. However, GL has distinct competitive advantages through its established position over 60+ years in the lower-middle to middle-income market with exclusive distribution channels.

risks.title: Regulatory Risk
risks.score_rationale: Regulatory risk is moderate due to potential regulatory changes in the insurance sector. No major changes were observed in 2025.

risks.title: Liquidity Risk
risks.score_rationale: Liquidity risk is low. GL has strong operating cash flows from insurance premiums and repurchased 5.4 million shares for $685 million in 2025.

ai_positioning.summary: GL does not mention artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar technologies in its 10-K/20-F filing. No references to AI are made in strategic, operational, or technological contexts.
